maria_cs: Customer reported a weird case where a handful of users were not removed from app roles after Okta SCIM deprovisioning yesterday. They see users still in the UI but Okta shows them removed. :thinking:

rory_eng: curious — any common trait for those users? same group, same externalId pattern?

maria_cs: all were in an LDAP-synced group that maps to two roles (admin + analyst) via our group-to-role mapper. group externalIds look like `ldap:dept/infra` for most.

jenna_support: do we have provisioning event logs for those users? can you paste the SCIM audit IDs or provisioning job id?

maria_cs: yes, provisioning job 2026-03-15-okta-push-4821. relevant events: `DELETE /Users/{id}` forwarded to us, we returned 200, but UI still shows the admin role attached.

rory_eng: hmm 200 on DELETE but role remains. two fast hypotheses: 1) we removed user object but didn't remove role bindings (separate write path), 2) race with our background role-resolution job that re-applied role because group membership lookup returned stale LDAP cache.

amir_sec: is the SCIM token scoped limited? if token only had user:write but not group:write or role:manage, we might return 200 for user deletion but skip role cleanup and still surface success to Okta.

maria_cs: good call — customer is using a scoped SCIM token they created with limited scopes. they said they used the token created by their SRE with the minimal checked boxes.

rory_eng: can you repro locally? steps I'll try: 1) create scoped token with only users:write, 2) Okta group-push removing user triggers `DELETE /Users/{id}`, 3) our handler runs user deletion path but role-unbind requires `POST /RoleBindings` deletion which checks token scopes. if token lacks `roles:write` we log a warning and skip.

rory_eng: sample curl to check token scopes:  
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/admin/scim/token_info
```
should list scopes.

jenna_support: customer sent the token_info output — scopes: `users:write groups:read` (no roles:write). that matches the hypothesis.

amir_sec: ok that's a security-by-design path — scoped tokens won't allow role modifications. But we should never leave orphaned admin appearances. we need an atomic operation or compensating cleanup job.

rory_eng: immediate mitigation: advise customer to create a SCIM token with `roles:write` or give our provisioning integration the `full-provisioning` preset. long term: add a server-side compensating job that looks for deleted users and cleans role bindings even if the original request token lacked roles scope (runs under system credentials).

maria_cs: enacted mitigation steps and customer confirmed manual token update. they also asked for a one-time cleanup run.

rory_eng: I'll run the cleanup with ops-bot. command I will run (system creds):
```
POST /internal/ops/cleanup-orphaned-role-bindings
Body: {"provisioning_job_id":"2026-03-15-okta-push-4821"}
```
expected: deletes any role_bindings referencing user ids removed in that job.

ops_bot: scheduled job started by rory_eng at 2987654327, job-id: cleanup-2987654327, ETA ~45s. :gear:

ops_bot: cleanup-2987654327 completed. removed 7 orphaned role bindings, 0 errors.

maria_cs: customer confirmed UI now shows users removed and roles cleaned. they asked what caused it so they can avoid it. I explained the token-scope limitation and recommended token preset.

amir_sec: can we add a KB article and a short console warning when a customer creates a scoped token without `roles:write` and also enables group-to-role mappings? that would prevent surprises.

rory_eng: yes. filed ENG ticket INF-1029 to add server-side compensating cleanup + console warning + KB. assigning to eng-runtime.

jenna_support: marking customer case as resolved and sending postmortem summary. :white_check_mark:

maria_cs: thanks team — good triage. tagging follow-ups: @rory_eng implement cleanup, @amir_sec add console warning content, @jenna_support send KB link to customer.

maria_cs: closing thread once the ENG ticket is referenced in the support case.
